column1: # Per-target fuzz budgets (cgz-7v2.4.4, shape fixed by cgz-r14 and
# docs/architecture/FUZZING.md).
# Columns are tab separated:
#   target  smoke_iterations  extended_iterations  min_covered_points
# target              Substring matching exactly one `test "fuzz: ..."` in
#                     tests/fuzz_targets.zig. tools/run-fuzz fails when a
#                     declared target has no row or a row matches no target, so
#                     adding a target without a budget is a failure rather than
#                     a target nobody fuzzes.
# smoke_iterations    The per-PR budget. Iterations, not wall clock, so it is
#                     reproducible across runners of differing speed.
# extended_iterations The scheduled-job budget.
# min_covered_points  Absolute instrumented points the smoke run must reach.
#                     The denominator changes as code grows, so an absolute
#                     numerator is the stable ratchet. A target that becomes
#                     validator-only loses covered points and fails.
# ## Why these numbers
# Measured on aarch64-macos, pinned toolchain, Debug: the generation target
# sustains roughly 10 runs per second, because every iteration lays out a
# molecule and then lays it out again to check determinism. 2000 smoke
# iterations is therefore about three and a half minutes per target, which is a
# PR-sized cost. The extended budget is an order of magnitude above it.
# The driver runs ReleaseSafe: Debug writes a zero-length coverage header on
# x86_64-linux for these multi-module targets, while ReleaseSafe preserves
# runtime safety checks and produces a valid coverage report on both targets.
# Fresh-cache x86_64-linux measurements on the pinned toolchain, 2026-08-30:
# generation reached 4700 points after its promoted cgz-7v2.34 regression was
# fixed; the other completed smoke runs reached hostile 1336, native domains
# 4286, C atom/bond 1804, and C extended 2667. Empty-corpus startup proved too
# variable for both C state targets: ownership measured as low as 340 on Linux,
# and atom/bond reached 1314 on macOS against its 1500 floor. A shared,
# structured valid-input bootstrap raised fresh-cache Linux measurements to
# 3517 (atom/bond) and 3420 (ownership) without lowering either floor. Floors
# retain headroom while still failing if a target collapses to its shallow
# validator path. Raising a floor follows observed growth; lowering one requires
# a new fresh-cache measurement and review.
# Raising a budget or coverage floor needs no justification. LOWERING either
# needs measured evidence and review, which is the point of recording them here
# rather than in a workflow file.
